Request was throttled, please try again later.
Unknown exception from EBT network

ErrorsArray.description: An array with information about the error.

code.description: A short string that represents the error.

message.description: A developer-facing message with more details about the error, not to be displayed to customers.

resource.description: The type of the Forage resource involved in the error.

ref.description: If applicable, the ten character reference hash of the Forage resource that caused the error. An empty string if no specific individual resource was involved.

details.description: Additional details about the error, if applicable.

ErrorResponseObject.description: An object that includes details about the error.

OrderPaymentRequest.description: This object represents a one-time payment, charged to a single payment method, associated with a specific Forage Order.

funding_type.description:
A string that represents the type of tender. One of:

- `benefit`
- `credit_tpp`
- `ebt_cash`
- `ebt_snap`

amount.description:
A positive decimal number that represents how much to charge the `PaymentMethod` in USD. Precision is supported to the penny.

This value must match the `ebt_cash_total` or `snap_total` value that was passed in the request that [created the Custom Capture Session](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-capture-session), depending on the `funding_type`.

If you need to charge both funding types, then create an `OrderPayment` for each charge, using the same `order_ref` returned when the order's parent [Payment Capture Session was created](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-capture-session).

The minimum amount that can be charged is `0.01`.

payment_method.description: The unique reference hash for the existing Forage [`PaymentMethod`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payment-methods) that is to be charged in this transaction.

merchant_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that should be restored to the merchant from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

platform_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that should be restored to the platform from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

ref.description:
A unique reference hash for the Forage `OrderPayment` object.

_Note:_ `receipt.ref_number` equals `ref`.

status.description:
The status of the `OrderPayment`. One of:

- `authorized`: The `OrderPayment` has been authorized, but not yet captured. Only applicable to HSA/FSA payments, which use an authorize-then-capture flow.
- `canceled`: The `OrderPayment` object can't be used.
- `failed`: If the error is temporary, then this `OrderPayment` can be resubmitted for capture without modification. Check the `receipt.message` field for a description of the error.
- `processing`: The outcome of the `OrderPayment` is pending.
- `requires_confirmation`: The `OrderPayment` hasn't been submitted for processing.
- `succeeded`: The `OrderPayment` has been successfully processed and will be included in settlement. It can't be changed.

last_processing_error.description: The code and message values corresponding to the most recent [Payments API error](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/errors#payments-api-errors).

created.description: A UTC timestamp, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string, of when the `OrderPayment` was created.

updated.description: A UTC timestamp, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string, of when the `OrderPayment` was last modified.

success_date.description: A UTC timestamp, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string, of when the `status` of the `OrderPayment` is `succeeded`. This value is always `null` when the `OrderPayment` is first created.

tpp_lookup_id.description:

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

patch.description:
> ⚠️ Update `OrderPayment` Server-Side Only
>
> To keep your app secure, requests to update an `OrderPayment` should only be generated on the server-side.

A `PATCH` request to `/orders/{order_ref}/payments/{payment_ref}/` updates an existing Forage `OrderPayment`.

On success, the API responds with the updated [OrderPayment](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/order-payments) object.

The `status` property of the `OrderPayment` determines what data can be updated. If the `status` is `processing`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`, then only the following `Payment` fields can be modified:

- `metadata`
- `external_order_id`

During these statuses, Forage ignores attempts to update other `OrderPayment` fields.

CustomerIDField.description:
**⚠️ If you’re integrating Forage with a POS Terminal, then do not use this param. It is only supported for online transactions.**

A unique identifier for the end customer making the payment.

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

post.description:
> ⚠️ `OrderPayment`` Updates Must Be Server-Side
>
> To keep your app secure, requests to cancel an OrderPayment should only be generated on the server-side.

A `POST` request to `/orders/{order_ref}/payments/{payment_ref}/cancel/` cancels an existing `OrderPayment`.

An `OrderPayment` can only be cancelled if its `status` is `requires_confirmation` or `failed`. Because only payments in these unsuccessful states can be canceled, this endpoint has no financial side effects.

On success, the API responds with the original `OrderPayment` object.

OrderPaymentRequest.description: This object represents a one-time payment, charged to a single payment method, associated with a specific Forage Order.

funding_type.description:
A string that represents the type of tender. One of:

- `benefit`
- `credit_tpp`
- `ebt_cash`
- `ebt_snap`

amount.description:
A positive decimal number that represents how much to charge the `PaymentMethod` in USD. Precision is supported to the penny.

This value must match the `ebt_cash_total` or `snap_total` value that was passed in the request that [created the Custom Capture Session](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-capture-session), depending on the `funding_type`.

If you need to charge both funding types, then create an `OrderPayment` for each charge, using the same `order_ref` returned when the order's parent [Payment Capture Session was created](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-capture-session).

platform_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that should be restored to the platform from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

- `canceled`: The `OrderPayment` object can't be used.
- `failed`: If the error is temporary, then this `OrderPayment` can be resubmitted for capture without modification. Check the `receipt.message` field for a description of the error.
- `processing`: The outcome of the `OrderPayment` is pending.
- `requires_confirmation`: The `OrderPayment` hasn't been submitted for processing.
- `succeeded`: The `OrderPayment` has been successfully processed and will be included in settlement. It can't be changed.

post.summary: Create a refund for an entire Order

code-samples.code:
curl --request POST \
    --url https://api.sandbox.joinforage.app/api/orders/<order_ref>/refund_all/ \
    --header 'Authorization: Bearer <api_key>' \
    --header 'Merchant-Account: <merchant-id>' \
    --header 'Idempotency-Key: <idempotency-key>' \
    --header 'accept: application/json' \
    --header 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data '
{
  "reason": "Order could not be delivered.",
  "metadata": {},
  "external_order_id": "<external-order-id>"
}
'

post.description:
> ⚠️ Refunding Entire Orders Must Be Server-Side
>
> To keep your app secure, requests to refund an entire Order should only be generated on the server-side.

A `POST` request to `/orders/{order_ref}/refund_all/` refunds an entire `Order`. It tells Forage’s servers to create an `OrderRefund` for every associated `OrderPayment`, and to refund all charges to their original payment methods, net any already processed refunds. This request has immediate financial side effects.

On success, the API responds with the original [`Order`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/orders). The `refunds` field details a list of reference hashes, `refund_refs`, for all of the `OrderRefunds` that Forage created as part of the refund process.

If there are any `OrderRefunds` still processing when you send the `POST`, then the API returns a `400` until those refunds have resolved.

To retrieve information about a particular `OrderRefund` in the list, send a `GET` to [`/orders/{order_ref}/refunds/{refund_ref}/`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/get-an-order-refund).

> ⚠️ Retrieving Refund Receipt Info
>
> This endpoint does not return `receipt` information.
>
> To retrieve transaction information to display to a customer, send periodic `GET` requests to `/orders/{order_ref}/refunds/{refund_ref}/` for every`OrderRefund` returned in the `refunds` field until the status of each is `succeeded`. Then, confirm that the `receipt.balance.updated` timestamp is no longer changing and retrieve the latest balance.

> 📘 Webhooks For Refund Status Updates
>
> Forage sends a `REFUND_STATUS_UPDATED` webhook when the status of a refund changes. Check out the [guide to Forage webhooks](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/configure-webhooks#refund_status_updated) for instructions on how to listen for the event.

ref.description: A unique reference hash for the Forage `Order` object.

snap_total.description: The SNAP eligible portion of the order cost in USD, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

ebt_cash_total.description: The portion of the `Order` total, in USD, that is EBT Cash eligible only, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

remaining_total.description: The portion of the `Order` total, in USD, that is neither SNAP eligible nor EBT Cash eligible, represented as a numeric string. This amount must be charged to a credit or debit card, with precision supported to the penny. _This value is returned only for [Fully Hosted Sessions](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/forage-sessions#fully-hosted-session) and is not included if the `Order` was created using a POST request to [`/capture_sessions/`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-capture-session)._

product_list.description: A list of the products in the customer's cart. If there are no taxes applied to any of the products, then this field can be empty. _This value is only returned for [Fully Hosted Sessions](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/forage-sessions#fully-hosted-session). It is not returned if the `Order` was created via a POST to [`/capture_sessions/`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-capture-session)._

platform_fee.description: An optional field, for use by a platform supporting multiple merchants, that indicates the percentage cut of each payment that the platform charges as a fee. Represented as a decimal string.

is_delivery.description: Whether the order is for delivery or pickup. This information is required per FNS regulations. Defaults to `false` if not provided.

success_redirect_url.description: The URL to redirect your customer to if the order is completed successfully, passed in the original request to create a `Session`.

cancel_redirect_url.description: The URL to redirect your customer to if they cancel the order, passed in the original request to create a `Session`.

supported_benefits.description: A list that limits the types of payment methods that can be applied at checkout, including any or all of the values in: `["snap", "ebt_cash", "non_ebt"]`. Use `supported_benefits` **only** if you want to restrict the possible payment method types. Omit this field in all other cases. For example, pass `["snap", "non_ebt"]` if you want to accept SNAP and credit card payments only (excluding EBT Cash).

psp_customer_id.description:
The third-party credit/debit payment processor's unique identifier for the customer. _This value is returned as `null` if the `Order` was created via a POST to [`/capture_sessions/`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-capture-session)._

**You must build with Forage Version `2023-05-15` or later to use `psp_customer_id`.** Either pass `2023-05-15` as the `API-Version` header on a per request basis, or set the version for all requests in the Forage dashboard.

external_location_id.description: A unique identifier for the physical fulfillment location.

status.description:
The status of the `Order` in the Forage lifecycle. One of:

- `canceled`
- `draft` (the status at the start, when a Session is created)
- `failed`
- `processing`
- `succeeded`

If the value is `failed`, then [inspect the associated Order Payments](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/get-all-order-payments) to determine the cause of the error.

payments.description: An array of the unique reference hashes for any Forage `OrderPayment` objects associated with the `Order`.

refunds.description: An array of the unique reference hashes for any Forage `OrderRefund` objects associated with the `Order`.

success_date.description: A UTC timestamp of the date when the `Order` was successfully charged. This value is `null` if the `status` of the `Order` is not yet `succeeded`.

receipt.description:
Most of the information that you're required to display to the customer, according to FNS regulations.

This field is `null` if the data that populates the receipt is not yet available.

The total amount paid by the customer is `snap_amount` + `ebt_cash_amount` + `other_amount`. This amount will be settled with the merchant after applying Forage's fees.

expires_at.description:
A UTC timestamp of when the `Order` will expire if it is not captured or canceled, set to 30 minutes from when the `Order` is created.

If the `status` of the `Order` is `succeeded` or `canceled`, then the `expires_at` value is `null`.

is_commercial_shipping.description: Whether the order is to be shipped commercially. FNS uses this value in its database for statistics.

BalanceResponse.description: An object that represents an EBT cardholder's account balance.

id.description: The unique identifier for the balance record.

snap.description: The available SNAP balance in USD on the customer’s EBT Card, represented as a numeric string.

non_snap.description: The available EBT Cash balance in USD on the customer's EBT Card, represented as a numeric string.

tax_rate.description: The tax rate applied to the item by the entity described in the `imposed_by` field, represented as a decimal string. If the product is subject to only one tax rate, then use the single `tax_rate` param instead of `tax_rate_list`.

taxes_charged.description: The portion of taxes charged for this item attributable to the `imposed_by` entity, represented as a numeric string.

taxes_exempted.description: The portion of taxes exempted for this item attributable to the `imposed_by` entity, represented as a numeric string.

eligibility.description: The eligibility of the product. Must be `snap`, `ebt_cash`, or `non_ebt`.

snap_amount.description: The amount paid for this product using SNAP benefits in USD, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

cash_amount.description: The amount paid for this product using EBT Cash benefits in USD, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

credit_debit_amount.description: The amount paid for this product using credit or debit card in USD, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

tax_collected.description: The tax amount collected for this product in USD, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

taxes_charged.description: The amount of taxes charged for this product in USD, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

taxes_exempted.description: The amount of taxes exempted for this product in USD, represented as a numeric string. Precision is supported to the penny.

⚠️ **Exception**: If the purchase is made in-store via a POS Terminal, then a `delivery_address` is not required when creating a `Payment`.

line2.description: The second line of the street address.

Most of the information that you're required to display to the customer, according to FNS regulations.

ebt_cash_amount.description: The USD amount charged/refunded to the EBT Cash balance of the EBT Card, represented as a numeric string.

other_amount.description: The USD amount charged/refunded to any payment method that is not an EBT Card, represented as a numeric string.

CustomerIDField.description:
**⚠️ If you’re integrating Forage with a POS Terminal, then do not use this param. It is only supported for online transactions.**

A unique identifier for the end customer making the payment.

Forage automatically adds the `customer_id` to the Session's corresponding `Order` and `OrderPayments`.

This field helps Forage's servers more quickly identify the customer associated with the request. While `customer_id` is not technically required, if you omit it then requests could take longer to process. **It is strongly recommended to pass customer_id.**

If you're providing your internal customer ID, then we recommend that you hash the value before sending it on the payload.

Each customer should only have one unique `customer_id`. For example, if you create both a `PaymentMethod` and a Forage `Session` (Fully Hosted or Custom) or `Payment` (SDK) for the same customer, then the `customer_id` should be the same in both requests to ensure continuity of stored payment methods.

A unique identifier for the order as created by the merchant or platform (not Forage).

When a merchant or platform passes this order ID to Forage, it persists in each Forage transaction related to the `Order`. This field enables merchants to map order IDs in their system to corresponding Forage `Order` IDs.

**You must build with Forage Version `2023-05-15` or later to use `external_order_id`.** Either pass `2023-05-15` as the `API-Version` header on a per request basis, or set the version for all requests in the Forage dashboard.

MetadataObject.description:
A required object containing merchant-defined key-value pairs to provide additional context for the payment.

Merchants should use this field to store **reference information** relevant to the transaction (for example, order details, system identifiers, or tracking data). This helps link the payment to records within their system.

Pass an empty object (`{}`) if no additional information is available.

> ⚠️ Personally Identifiable Information
>
> **Do not include personally identifiable information (PII)** such as names, emails, or payment details.

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

post.summary: Create refunds for specific products in an Order
post.description:
> ⚠️ Product Refunds Must Be Server-Side
>
> To keep your app secure, requests to refund specific products should only be generated on the server-side.

A `POST` request to `/orders/{order_ref}/refund_by_product/` creates refunds for specific products in an `Order`. It tells Forage's servers to create `OrderRefund` objects for the specified products and refund the appropriate amounts to their original payment methods. This request has immediate financial side effects.

On success, the API responds with an array of refund objects that represent the transactions and a `201` HTTP status code.

### HTTP STATUS 201

This endpoint always returns a `201`, even if some refund attempts fail, because Forage always creates refund objects to preserve a record of the attempted transactions. To make sure that the refunds were successful, check that the `status` of each refund is `succeeded`. Send periodic `GET` requests to `/orders/{order_ref}/refunds/{refund_ref}/` to retrieve the updated objects. If the status is `failed`, then inspect the `last_processing_error` field of the response object for information about the error.

> 📘 Webhooks For Refund Status Updates
>
> Forage sends a `REFUND_STATUS_UPDATED` webhook when the status of a refund changes. Check out the [guide to Forage webhooks](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/configure-webhooks#refund_status_updated) for instructions on how to listen for the event.

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

The total amount paid by the customer is `snap_amount` + `ebt_cash_amount` + `other_amount`. This amount will be settled with the merchant after applying Forage's fees.

ref_number.description:
A unique reference hash for the Forage `Order`, `Payment`, or `Refund` associated with this receipt.

Note: `receipt.ref_number` equals `ref`.

is_voided.description: Whether the transaction associated with this receipt has been voided. If `false`, then the transaction finished processing as expected. If `true`, then the transaction was reversed.

snap_amount.description: The USD amount charged/refunded to the SNAP balance of the EBT Card, represented as a numeric string.

ebt_cash_amount.description: The USD amount charged/refunded to the EBT Cash balance of the EBT Card, represented as a numeric string.

cash_back_amount.description: The USD amount of cash back given to the customer, represented as a numeric string.

other_amount.description: The USD amount charged/refunded to any payment method that is not an EBT Card, represented as a numeric string.

sales_tax_applied.description: The USD amount of taxes charged to the customer’s non-EBT payment instrument, represented as a numeric string.

last_4.description: The last four digits of the EBT Card number.

message.description: A message from the EBT payment network that must be displayed to the EBT cardholder.

transaction_type.description: A constant string that is used to identify the transaction type associated with the receipt.

created.description: A UTC timestamp of when the Forage transaction object was created, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string.

sequence_number.description: The terminal transaction sequence number for POS transactions. `null` for online (non-POS) transactions.

ExternalOrderIDField.description:
A unique identifier for the order as created by the merchant or platform (not Forage).

When a merchant or platform passes this order ID to Forage, it persists in each Forage transaction related to the `Order`. This field enables merchants to map order IDs in their system to corresponding Forage `Order` IDs.

**You must build with Forage Version `2023-05-15` or later to use `external_order_id`.** Either pass `2023-05-15` as the `API-Version` header on a per request basis, or set the version for all requests in the Forage dashboard.

MetadataObject.description:
A required object containing merchant-defined key-value pairs to provide additional context for the payment.

Merchants should use this field to store **reference information** relevant to the transaction (for example, order details, system identifiers, or tracking data). This helps link the payment to records within their system.

Pass an empty object (`{}`) if no additional information is available.

> ⚠️ Personally Identifiable Information
>
> **Do not include personally identifiable information (PII)** such as names, emails, or payment details.

AuthenticationBearerTokenHeader.name: Authorization
AuthenticationBearerTokenHeader.description: An OAuth 2.0 [authentication token](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/authentication#authentication-tokens) that validates the request. Send a `POST` to the [`/o/token/`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-authentication-token) endpoint to generate an authentication token. Pass the token in this header after the word `Bearer` and a whitespace, for example `Bearer <api_key>`.

MerchantAccountHeader.name: Merchant-Account
MerchantAccountHeader.description: A unique merchant ID that Forage provides during onboarding, as in `123ab45c67`. The Merchant ID can be found in the Forage [sandbox](https://dashboard.sandbox.joinforage.app/login/) or [production](https://dashboard.joinforage.app/login/) dashboard.

APIVersionHeader.name: API-Version
APIVersionHeader.description:
The [Forage version](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/version-history), represented as a string with the format of a `YYYY-MM-DD` date.

If not specified in the request header, then the version defaults to the value set in the Forage dashboard.

OAuth2.description: Pass the access token in the 'Authorization' header with the format "Bearer ${token}", i.e. the word "Bearer" and your access token from the /o/token/ API, separated by whitespace.

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

post.description:
> ⚠️ Payment Creation Must Be Server-Side
>
> To keep your app secure, requests to create a Payment should only be generated on the server-side.

A `POST` request to `/payments/` tells Forage’s servers how much to charge an existing `PaymentMethod`.

On success, the API responds with a Forage `Payment` object that represents the one-time charge. You need to pass the `ref` response value to an SDK function to authorize and capture the payment, one of:

- Forage JS: [`capturePayment()`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/capture-ebt-payment)
- Android: [`capturePayment()`](https://android.joinforage.app/forage-android/com.joinforage.forage.android.ecom.services/-forage-s-d-k/capture-payment)
- iOS: [`capturePayment()`](https://github.com/teamforage/forage-ios-sdk?tab=readme-ov-file#capture-an-ebt-payment)

> 📘 Use `customer_id` When Creating Payments
>
> Pass `customer_id` in the request to Create a `Payment`. `customer_id` helps Forage's servers more quickly identify and associate the correct customer with the `Payment`. While `customer_id` is not technically a required parameter, if you omit it then the request to create the `Payment` could take longer to process. **It is strongly recommended to pass `customer_id`.**
>
> Each customer should only have one unique `customer_id`. For example, if you create both a `Payment` and a `PaymentMethod` for the same customer, then the `customer_id` should be the same in both requests to ensure continuity of stored payment methods.

> ⚠️ Payments Expire After 30 Minutes
>
> `Payment` objects expire after 30 minutes. If a `Payment` is not captured or canceled within 30 minutes of when it's created, then it expires. To attempt the transaction again, create a new `Payment`.

ErrorsArray.description: An array with information about the error.

code.description: A short string that represents the error.

message.description: A developer-facing message with more details about the error, not to be displayed to customers.

resource.description: The type of the Forage resource involved in the error.

ref.description: If applicable, the ten character reference hash of the Forage resource that caused the error. An empty string if no specific individual resource was involved.

details.description: Additional details about the error, if applicable.

ErrorResponseObject.description: An object that includes details about the error.

PaymentRequest.description: This object represents a single payment. It is associated with a single payment method.

amount.description: A positive decimal number that represents how much to charge the [`PaymentMethod`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payment-methods) in USD. Precision is supported to the penny. The minimum amount that can be charged is `0.01`. To differentiate between a SNAP and an EBT Cash charge on the same EBT Card, use the `funding_type` field. If you need to charge both funding types, then create a `Payment` for each charge.

funding_type.description: The payment instrument type. Use this field to differentiate between a SNAP (`ebt_snap`) and an EBT Cash (`ebt_cash`) charge on the same EBT Card. If you need to charge both funding types, then create a `Payment` for each charge. Use `credit_payfac` for all charges to HSA/FSA cards. `credit_tpp` is the funding type assigned to non-EBT payment objects created via a Fully Hosted Checkout integration.

payment_method.description:
The unique reference hash for the existing Forage [`PaymentMethod`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payment-methods) that is to be charged in this transaction.

⚠️ **Exception**: POS integrations do not need to provide a `payment_method` when creating a payment.

is_delivery.description:
⚠️ **Exception**: If the purchase is made in-store via a POS Terminal, then a `is_delivery` is not required when creating a `Payment`.

Whether the order is for delivery or pickup. This information is required per FNS regulations. Defaults to `false` if not provided.

platform_fee.description: An optional field, for use by a platform supporting multiple merchants, that indicates the percentage cut of each payment that the platform charges as a fee.

platform_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that a platform takes from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

merchant_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that should be restored to the merchant from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

tpp_lookup_id.description:
An identifier for the credit/debit TPP.

For Stripe integrations, the client secret for a Stripe `PaymentIntent`.

merchant_destination_account.description:
A unique reference hash for the bank account that is to receive funds settlement for this payment. Use this field if you're settling funds across multiple merchant bank accounts. Reach out to your Forage account manager for details on generating a hash.

Defaults to the hash for the default merchant bank account if not provided.

pos_terminal.description:
**⚠️  This param is only supported for POS Terminal integrations. Do not use this param for online transactions.**

An object that details information about the POS Terminal that processes the payment.

provider_terminal_id.description: A unique string that identifies the POS Terminal.

ref.description:
A unique reference hash for the Forage `Payment` object.

_Note:_ `receipt.ref_number` equals `ref`.

You need to pass this value to the front-end SDK method that captures the payment.

merchant.description: A string that represents a unique merchant ID that Forage provides during onboarding.

status.description:
The status of the `Payment`. One of:

- `canceled`: The `Payment`object can't be used.
- `failed`: If the error is temporary, then this `Payment` can be resubmitted for capture without modification. Check the `receipt.message` field for a description of the error.
- `processing`: The outcome of the `Payment` is pending.
- `requires_confirmation`: The `Payment` hasn't been submitted for processing.
- `succeeded`: The `Payment` has been successfully processed and will be included in settlement. It can't be changed.
- `authorized`: The `Payment` has been authorized, but not yet captured. Only applicable to HSA payments.

created.description: A UTC timestamp of when the `Payment` was created, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string.

updated.description: A UTC timestamp of that indicates when the `Payment` was last modified, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string.

expires_at.description:
A UTC timestamp of when the `Payment` will expire if it is not captured or canceled, set to 30 minutes from when the `Payment` is created.

If the `status` of the `Payment` is `succeeded` or `canceled`, then the `expires_at` value is `null`.

success_date.description: A UTC timestamp of when the `Payment` was successfully processed, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string. This value is `null` until the Payment enters the `succeeded` or `partial_capture` states.

refunds.description:
References to the `Refund`s attached to this payment. The format depends on the `with_refunds` query parameter:

- **Default behavior** (when `with_refunds` is `false` or omitted): Array of refund reference strings
- **Expanded behavior** (when `with_refunds=true`): Array of full `Refund` objects with complete refund details

receipt.description:
Most of the information that you're required to display to the customer, according to FNS regulations.

This field is `null` if the data that populates the receipt is not yet available.

The total amount paid by the customer is `snap_amount` + `ebt_cash_amount` + `other_amount`. This amount will be settled with the merchant after applying Forage's fees.

last_processing_error.description: The `code` and `message` values corresponding to the most recent [Payments API error](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/errors#payments-api-errors). Always `null` when the `Payment` is created.

address_postal_code_check.description:
The result of any check done on the delivery address zip code. One of:
- `pass`: The provided information is correct and matches the data on file with the card issuer.
- `fail`: The provided information is incorrect and does not match the data on file.
- `unavailable`: The card issuer will not perform the check.
- `unchecked`: The information was provided but has not yet been checked by the card issuer.

cvc_check.description:
The result of any check done on the CVC. One of:
- `pass`: The provided information is correct and matches the data on file with the card issuer.
- `fail`: The provided information is incorrect and does not match the data on file.
- `unavailable`: The card issuer will not perform the check.
- `unchecked`: The information was provided but has not yet been checked by the card issuer.

delivery_address.description: The delivery or pickup address for the order, passed to the EBT network. Returns an address object with `line1`, `line2`, `city`, `state`, `zipcode`, and `country`. Null when no delivery address is set.

is_delivery.description: Whether the order is for delivery or pickup. Null when not specified.

DeliveryAddressData.description:
⚠️ **Exception**: If the purchase is made in-store via a POS Terminal, then a `delivery_address` is not required when creating a `Payment`.

The address for delivery or pickup of the `Order`. Per FNS regulations, this value must always be provided. If the `Order` is for pickup, then use the merchant address.

country.description: Either `us` or `US`. Defaults to `US` if not provided.

line1.description: The first line of the street address.

line2.description: The second line of the street address.

state.description: The two-letter abbreviation, can be upper or lowercase, for the US state.

CustomerIDField.description:
**⚠️ If you’re integrating Forage with a POS Terminal, then do not use this param. It is only supported for online transactions.**

A unique identifier for the end customer making the payment.

Forage automatically adds the `customer_id` to the Session's corresponding `Order` and `OrderPayments`.

This field helps Forage's servers more quickly identify the customer associated with the request. While `customer_id` is not technically required, if you omit it then requests could take longer to process. **It is strongly recommended to pass customer_id.**

If you're providing your internal customer ID, then we recommend that you hash the value before sending it on the payload.

Each customer should only have one unique `customer_id`. For example, if you create both a `PaymentMethod` and a Forage `Session` (Fully Hosted or Custom) or `Payment` (SDK) for the same customer, then the `customer_id` should be the same in both requests to ensure continuity of stored payment methods.

ExternalOrderIDField.description:
A unique identifier for the order as created by the merchant or platform (not Forage).

When a merchant or platform passes this order ID to Forage, it persists in each Forage transaction related to the `Order`. This field enables merchants to map order IDs in their system to corresponding Forage `Order` IDs.

**You must build with Forage Version `2023-05-15` or later to use `external_order_id`.** Either pass `2023-05-15` as the `API-Version` header on a per request basis, or set the version for all requests in the Forage dashboard.

ExternalLocationIDField.description: A unique identifier, provided by the merchant or platform (not Forage), that indicates the physical fulfillment location for the order. For example, this field could specify which location of a grocery store chain fulfilled an order.

MetadataObject.description:
A required object containing merchant-defined key-value pairs to provide additional context for the payment.

Merchants should use this field to store **reference information** relevant to the transaction (for example, order details, system identifiers, or tracking data). This helps link the payment to records within their system.

Pass an empty object (`{}`) if no additional information is available.

> ⚠️ Personally Identifiable Information
>
> **Do not include personally identifiable information (PII)** such as names, emails, or payment details.

parameters.name: external_order_id
parameters.description:
A unique, merchant or platform-provided identifier for the order that corresponds to their own database, as provided in the original request to [create the `Payment`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-a-payment).

Only one `external_order_id` can be passed as a query param at a time.

**You must build with Forage Version `2023-05-15` or later to use `external_order_id`.** Either pass `2023-05-15` as the `API-Version` header on a per request basis, or set the version for all requests in the Forage dashboard.

parameters.name: with_refunds
parameters.description:
Include this parameter to expand the `refunds` list to full `Refund` objects. This provides complete refund details including amount, status, reason, and other refund-specific information.

If omitted, the `refunds` field contains only refund reference strings. Pass as `&with_refunds` (no value needed). Examples may show `with_refunds=true` for clarity, but only the presence of the parameter is required.

get.summary: Retrieve all Payments for a merchant order ID
get.description:
A `GET` request to `/payments/` that includes the `external_order_id` query param retrieves a list of all of the `Payment`s related to the order. The `external_order_id` corresponds to a merchant or platform's identifier for the order in their own database. Forage does not provide this value.

If a customer charges both SNAP and EBT Cash at checkout, then this endpoint could be useful to review the spending breakdown across `Payment` types.

**Refund details:** By default, the `refunds` field contains only refund reference strings. Include `with_refunds` to get complete refund information. You can pass it as `&with_refunds` (no `=true` required).

updated.description: A UTC timestamp of that indicates when the `Payment` was last modified, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string.

Most of the information that you're required to display to the customer, according to FNS regulations.

The result of any check done on the delivery address zip code. One of:
- `pass`: The provided information is correct and matches the data on file with the card issuer.
- `fail`: The provided information is incorrect and does not match the data on file.
- `unavailable`: The card issuer will not perform the check.
- `unchecked`: The information was provided but has not yet been checked by the card issuer.

is_delivery.description: Whether the order is for delivery or pickup. Null when not specified.

DeliveryAddressData.description:
⚠️ **Exception**: If the purchase is made in-store via a POS Terminal, then a `delivery_address` is not required when creating a `Payment`.

line1.description: The first line of the street address.

line2.description: The second line of the street address.

CustomerIDField.description:
**⚠️ If you’re integrating Forage with a POS Terminal, then do not use this param. It is only supported for online transactions.**

A unique identifier for the end customer making the payment.

Forage automatically adds the `customer_id` to the Session's corresponding `Order` and `OrderPayments`.

This field helps Forage's servers more quickly identify the customer associated with the request. While `customer_id` is not technically required, if you omit it then requests could take longer to process. **It is strongly recommended to pass customer_id.**

If you're providing your internal customer ID, then we recommend that you hash the value before sending it on the payload.

Each customer should only have one unique `customer_id`. For example, if you create both a `PaymentMethod` and a Forage `Session` (Fully Hosted or Custom) or `Payment` (SDK) for the same customer, then the `customer_id` should be the same in both requests to ensure continuity of stored payment methods.

A unique identifier for the order as created by the merchant or platform (not Forage).

When a merchant or platform passes this order ID to Forage, it persists in each Forage transaction related to the `Order`. This field enables merchants to map order IDs in their system to corresponding Forage `Order` IDs.

ExternalLocationIDField.description: A unique identifier, provided by the merchant or platform (not Forage), that indicates the physical fulfillment location for the order. For example, this field could specify which location of a grocery store chain fulfilled an order.

MetadataObject.description:
A required object containing merchant-defined key-value pairs to provide additional context for the payment.

Merchants should use this field to store **reference information** relevant to the transaction (for example, order details, system identifiers, or tracking data). This helps link the payment to records within their system.

Pass an empty object (`{}`) if no additional information is available.

> ⚠️ Personally Identifiable Information
>
> **Do not include personally identifiable information (PII)** such as names, emails, or payment details.

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

code-samples.code:
curl --request POST \
    --url https://api.sandbox.joinforage.app/api/payments/cc3175bfea/capture_payment/ \
    --header 'Authorization: Bearer <api_key>' \
    --header 'Merchant-Account: <merchant-id>' \
    --header 'Idempotency-Key: <idempotency-key>' \
    --header 'accept: application/json' \
    --header 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data '{
  "capture_amount": 11.98,
  "qualified_healthcare_total": 11.98,
  "qualified_healthcare_subtotal": 11.98,
  "product_list": [
    {
      "gtin": "00041260013003",
      "name": "Sample Healthcare Product",
      "unit_price": 5.99,
      "quantity": 2,
      "eligibility": "hsa_fsa"
    }
  ]
}
'

> 📘 Forage SDK Integrations And HSA/FSA Only
>
> This endpoint is only relevant to Forage SDK integrations and HSA/FSA payments.
>
> Instead of calling a front-end SDK method to capture a payment, you can use this endpoint to capture a payment from the backend.

A `POST` request to `/payments/{payment_ref}/capture_payment/` captures an existing Forage Payment.

On success, Forage automatically begins processing the charge to the customer, so this endpoint has immediate financial side effects.

The API responds with a [Payment](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payments) object that represents the transaction. For EBT payments the response also includes complete `receipt` information.

For HSA/FSA payments, the `capture_amount` must be less than or equal to the original `amount` field in the `Payment` object.

> ⚠️ Incompatible Fields for EBT Transactions
>
> Avoid using `capture_amount`, `qualified_healthcare_total`, `qualified_healthcare_subtotal`, and `product_list`. Including these fields in EBT transactions may cause unexpected behavior.

Once an HSA/FSA payment is captured, the `amount` field in the `Payment` object is updated to match the `capture_amount`. The originally authorized amount moves to the `authorization_amount` field, which is used only for debugging and bookkeeping.

> ⚠️ Capture Requests Must Be Server-Side
>
> To keep your app secure, requests to capture a payment should only be generated from the server-side.

The status of the `Payment`. One of:

CustomerIDField.description:
**⚠️ If you’re integrating Forage with a POS Terminal, then do not use this param. It is only supported for online transactions.**

A unique identifier for the end customer making the payment.

Forage automatically adds the `customer_id` to the Session's corresponding `Order` and `OrderPayments`.

This field helps Forage's servers more quickly identify the customer associated with the request. While `customer_id` is not technically required, if you omit it then requests could take longer to process. **It is strongly recommended to pass customer_id.**

If you're providing your internal customer ID, then we recommend that you hash the value before sending it on the payload.

Each customer should only have one unique `customer_id`. For example, if you create both a `PaymentMethod` and a Forage `Session` (Fully Hosted or Custom) or `Payment` (SDK) for the same customer, then the `customer_id` should be the same in both requests to ensure continuity of stored payment methods.

ExternalOrderIDField.description:
A unique identifier for the order as created by the merchant or platform (not Forage).

When a merchant or platform passes this order ID to Forage, it persists in each Forage transaction related to the `Order`. This field enables merchants to map order IDs in their system to corresponding Forage `Order` IDs.

**You must build with Forage Version `2023-05-15` or later to use `external_order_id`.** Either pass `2023-05-15` as the `API-Version` header on a per request basis, or set the version for all requests in the Forage dashboard.

ExternalLocationIDField.description: A unique identifier, provided by the merchant or platform (not Forage), that indicates the physical fulfillment location for the order. For example, this field could specify which location of a grocery store chain fulfilled an order.

MetadataObject.description:
A required object containing merchant-defined key-value pairs to provide additional context for the payment.

Merchants should use this field to store **reference information** relevant to the transaction (for example, order details, system identifiers, or tracking data). This helps link the payment to records within their system.

Pass an empty object (`{}`) if no additional information is available.

> ⚠️ Personally Identifiable Information
>
> **Do not include personally identifiable information (PII)** such as names, emails, or payment details.

CapturePayment.description: A request body to pass to `/payments/{payment_ref}/capture_payment/`. Required for HSA/FSA payments.

AuthenticationBearerTokenHeader.name: Authorization
AuthenticationBearerTokenHeader.description: An OAuth 2.0 [authentication token](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/authentication#authentication-tokens) that validates the request. Send a `POST` to the [`/o/token/`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-authentication-token) endpoint to generate an authentication token. Pass the token in this header after the word `Bearer` and a whitespace, for example `Bearer <api_key>`.

MerchantAccountHeader.name: Merchant-Account
MerchantAccountHeader.description: A unique merchant ID that Forage provides during onboarding, as in `123ab45c67`. The Merchant ID can be found in the Forage [sandbox](https://dashboard.sandbox.joinforage.app/login/) or [production](https://dashboard.joinforage.app/login/) dashboard.

IdempotencyKeyHeader.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyHeader.description: An alphanumeric key that clients can use to identify repeated requests that are dropped in transit. Generate a distinct key for every unique request and only re-use keys for retries.

APIVersionHeader.name: API-Version
APIVersionHeader.description:
The [Forage version](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/version-history), represented as a string with the format of a `YYYY-MM-DD` date.

If not specified in the request header, then the version defaults to the value set in the Forage dashboard.

OAuth2.description: Pass the access token in the 'Authorization' header with the format "Bearer ${token}", i.e. the word "Bearer" and your access token from the /o/token/ API, separated by whitespace.

scopes.hosted_checkout: Scope for tokens used by merchant applications which allow Forage to manage split tender processing (i.e. EBT + Credit/Debit).
scopes.pinpad_only: Scope for tokens used by merchant applications which manage their own split tender (i.e. Forage Checkout is used only for EBT processing).

scopes.internal: Scope for tokens used by Forage internal applications.
scopes.pin-protected: Scope for tokens which can access secure storage.
scopes.disbursement: Scope for tokens which can disburse money to merchants.

BearerAuth.description: Pass the access token in the 'Authorization' header with the format "Bearer ${token}", i.e. the word "Bearer" and your JWT bearer token from the /api/session_token/ end-point, separated by whitespace.

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

parameters.name: payment_ref
parameters.description: A unique reference hash for the Forage Payment object, returned when the [Payment was created](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/create-a-payment).

patch.description:
> ⚠️ Update Payment Requests Server-Side
>
> To keep your app secure, requests to update a `Payment` should only be generated on the server-side.

A `PATCH` request to `/payments/{payment_ref}/` updates an existing Forage `Payment`.

On success, the API responds with the updated [Payment](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payments) object.

The `status` property of the `Payment` determines what data can be updated. If the `status` is `processing`, `cancelled`, or `succeeded`, then only the following `Payment` fields can be modified:

- `metadata`
- `external_order_id`

During these statuses, Forage ignores attempts to update other `Payment` fields.

> 📘 Required For Server-Side Capture
>
> You need to use this endpoint if you're building an integration that [defers payment capture to the server](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/capture-ebt-payments-server-side).

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

PaymentRequest.description: This object represents a single payment. It is associated with a single payment method.

amount.description: A positive decimal number that represents how much to charge the [`PaymentMethod`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payment-methods) in USD. merchant_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that should be restored to the merchant from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

tpp_lookup_id.description:
An identifier for the credit/debit TPP.

For Stripe integrations, the client secret for a Stripe `PaymentIntent`.

merchant_destination_account.description:
A unique reference hash for the bank account that is to receive funds settlement for this payment. Use this field if you're settling funds across multiple merchant bank accounts. Reach out to your Forage account manager for details on generating a hash.

pos_terminal.description:
**⚠️  This param is only supported for POS Terminal integrations. Do not use this param for online transactions.**

An object that details information about the POS Terminal that processes the payment.

provider_terminal_id.description: A unique string that identifies the POS Terminal.

ref.description:
A unique reference hash for the Forage `Payment` object.

_Note:_ `receipt.ref_number` equals `ref`.

You need to pass this value to the front-end SDK method that captures the payment.

merchant.description: A string that represents a unique merchant ID that Forage provides during onboarding.

status.description:
The status of the `Payment`. One of:

- `canceled`: The `Payment`object can't be used.
- `failed`: If the error is temporary, then this `Payment` can be resubmitted for capture without modification. Check the `receipt.message` field for a description of the error.
- `processing`: The outcome of the `Payment` is pending.
- `requires_confirmation`: The `Payment` hasn't been submitted for processing.
- `succeeded`: The `Payment` has been successfully processed and will be included in settlement. It can't be changed.
- `authorized`: The `Payment` has been authorized, but not yet captured. Only applicable to HSA payments.

created.description: A UTC timestamp of when the `Payment` was created, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string.

updated.description: A UTC timestamp of that indicates when the `Payment` was last modified, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string.

expires_at.description:
A UTC timestamp of when the `Payment` will expire if it is not captured or canceled, set to 30 minutes from when the `Payment` is created.

If the `status` of the `Payment` is `succeeded` or `canceled`, then the `expires_at` value is `null`.

success_date.description: A UTC timestamp of when the `Payment` was successfully processed, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string. This value is `null` until the Payment enters the `succeeded` or `partial_capture` states.

refunds.description:
References to the `Refund`s attached to this payment. The format depends on the `with_refunds` query parameter:

- **Default behavior** (when `with_refunds` is `false` or omitted): Array of refund reference strings
- **Expanded behavior** (when `with_refunds=true`): Array of full `Refund` objects with complete refund details

Most of the information that you're required to display to the customer, according to FNS regulations.

This field is `null` if the data that populates the receipt is not yet available.

The total amount paid by the customer is `snap_amount` + `ebt_cash_amount` + `other_amount`. This amount will be settled with the merchant after applying Forage's fees.

- `unavailable`: The card issuer will not perform the check.
- `unchecked`: The information was provided but has not yet been checked by the card issuer.

- `unavailable`: The card issuer will not perform the check.
- `unchecked`: The information was provided but has not yet been checked by the card issuer.

post.description:
A `POST` request to `/payments/{payment_ref}/cancel/` stops an existing [`Payment` object](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payments#payment-object) from being submitted for capture in future API calls.

For EBT Payments, a `Payment` can only be canceled if its `status` is `requires_confirmation` or `failed`. For HSA/FSA payments, the `Payment` can only be canceled if its `status` is `authorized`.

If you need to charge both funding types, then create a `Payment` for each charge. Use `credit_payfac` for all charges to HSA/FSA cards. `credit_tpp` is the funding type assigned to non-EBT payment objects created via a Fully Hosted Checkout integration.

payment_method.description:
The unique reference hash for the existing Forage [`PaymentMethod`](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payment-methods) that is to be charged in this transaction.

⚠️ **Exception**: POS integrations do not need to provide a `payment_method` when creating a payment.

⚠️ **Exception**: If the purchase is made in-store via a POS Terminal, then a `is_delivery` is not required when creating a `Payment`.

Whether the order is for delivery or pickup. This information is required per FNS regulations. Defaults to `false` if not provided.

platform_fee.description: An optional field, for use by a platform supporting multiple merchants, that indicates the percentage cut of each payment that the platform charges as a fee.

platform_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that a platform takes from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

merchant_fixed_settlement.description: The fixed amount in USD that should be restored to the merchant from EBT Cash payments prior to splitting by the `platform_fee`. Precision is supported to the penny.

tpp_lookup_id.description:
An identifier for the credit/debit TPP.

merchant_destination_account.description:
A unique reference hash for the bank account that is to receive funds settlement for this payment. Use this field if you're settling funds across multiple merchant bank accounts. Reach out to your Forage account manager for details on generating a hash.

pos_terminal.description:
**⚠️  This param is only supported for POS Terminal integrations. Do not use this param for online transactions.**

An object that details information about the POS Terminal that processes the payment.

ref.description:

merchant.description: A string that represents a unique merchant ID that Forage provides during onboarding.

status.description:
The status of the `Payment`. One of:

updated.description: A UTC timestamp of that indicates when the `Payment` was last modified, represented as an [ISO 8601 date-time](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html) string.

**⚠️ If you’re integrating Forage with a POS Terminal, then do not use this param. It is only supported for online transactions.**

A unique identifier for the end customer making the payment.

A unique identifier for the order as created by the merchant or platform (not Forage).

When a merchant or platform passes this order ID to Forage, it persists in each Forage transaction related to the `Order`. This field enables merchants to map order IDs in their system to corresponding Forage `Order` IDs.

>

info.title: Forage Payments API
info.description:
The Forage Payments API is a REST API for processing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) payments (SNAP and EBT Cash) in your e-commerce or in-store application.

Processing any EBT payment, or checking an EBT card's balance, requires the cardholder's PIN. Federal regulations require all PIN entry to happen through a PCI-compliant, USDA-approved interface. Forage provides that interface, so EBT PIN collection always happens through a Forage-hosted surface (Forage Checkout or a Forage SDK), never directly in your own form. Some endpoints (for example, capture and balance) are only reachable through that surface because they require PIN data in the request.

EBT rarely covers an entire order: items like delivery fees and non-eligible products can't be paid with SNAP or EBT Cash. You decide how to handle the remaining balance (split tender) and any credit or debit processing alongside the EBT portion.

Forage offers four integration options. Pick the one that fits your platform and engineering resources:

1. **Fully Hosted Checkout.** Forage processes EBT and credit/debit through a Forage-hosted Checkout UI. Lowest engineering effort, and Forage absorbs most error handling. See the [Fully Hosted Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/fully-hosted).
2. **Custom Checkout.** Forage processes EBT; you handle split tender, taxes, and credit/debit in your own checkout flow. Best when you want minimal changes to your existing UX. See the [Custom Checkout guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/custom).
3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
4. **POS Terminal SDK.** Accept in-person EBT payments on an Android POS device. See the [POS Terminal guide](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-terminal-android).

As a general principle, any data created by your requests, or by your customers on a Forage-hosted surface, is retrievable through GET requests to the appropriate resource.

Have more questions? Use our [contact form](https://www.joinforage.com/get-in-touch) to reach our sales and engineering support teams.

post.description:
> ⚠️ HSA/FSA Payments Only

A `POST` request to `/payments/{payment_ref}/authorize/` performs an Authorization on an existing [`Payment` object](https://docs.joinforage.app/reference/payments#payment-object).

A hold will be placed on the cardholder's account for the `amount` of the payment. This hold will appear on the cardholder's statement as a pending transaction.
If `request_partial_authorization` is `true` then the amount authorized may be less then the original payment `amount`.
In this case the original `amount` is moved into a field `requested_amount` and the actual amount authorized will be in field `amount`.

3. **Online SDKs.** Client-side SDKs for [web](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/forage-js), [iOS](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/ios), and [Android](https://docs.joinforage.app/docs/android) that collect EBT PINs in your app while keeping you out of PCI scope.
